explanation: Read each BST in sorted inorder order, merge the sequences without removing duplicates, then build from half-open ranges. Choosing start+(end−start)/2 exactly matches the required structural convention.
timeComplexity: O(m+n) Inorder reads, merging and midpoint construction are each linear in total nodes.
spaceComplexity: O(m+n), including merged values and output nodes Value sequences and newly allocated result nodes are linear in total input size.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Inorder traversals produce the two sorted multisets. Standard merging preserves every occurrence. Recursive reconstruction chooses exactly the prescribed midpoint of each half-open range, so both the sorted contents and the required canonical structure follow.
walkthrough: The BSTs [4,1,7] and [6,2,9] merge to [1,2,4,6,7,9]. Midpoint construction gives root 6, left subtree rooted at 2 and right subtree rooted at 9. Level order is [6,2,9,1,4,7].
edgeCases: Either input tree may be empty.
Duplicate values from either input are retained.
The midpoint convention matters because this corpus compares structure.
